CVE-2025-31483.title: Miniflux is a feed reader. Due to a weak Content Security Policy  ...
CVE-2025-31483.description: Miniflux is a feed reader. Due to a weak Content Security Policy on the /proxy/* route, an attacker can bypass the CSP of the media proxy and execute cross-site scripting when opening external images in a new tab/window. To mitigate the vulnerability, the CSP for the media proxy has been changed from default-src 'self' to default-src 'none'; form-action 'none'; sandbox;. This vulnerability is fixed in 2.2.7.

CVE-2025-67713.title: Miniflux 2 is an open source feed reader. Versions 2.2.14 and bel ...
CVE-2025-67713.description: Miniflux 2 is an open source feed reader. Versions 2.2.14 and below treat redirect_url as safe when url.Parse(...).IsAbs() is false, enabling phishing flows after login. Protocol-relative URLs like //ikotaslabs.com have an empty scheme and pass that check, allowing post-login redirects to attacker-controlled sites. This issue is fixed in version 2.2.15.

CVE-2026-108735.title: Miniflux 2.3.0 through 2.3.3 contains a server-side request forge ...
CVE-2026-108735.description: Miniflux 2.3.0 through 2.3.3 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated users to reach internal addresses by setting a feed's proxy_url. Attackers can point proxy_url at loopback or internal hosts, bypassing FETCHER_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORKS checks to probe internal ports and send proxy-style requests to internal services.

CVE-2026-128330.title: Miniflux before 2.3.5 contains an insufficient session expiration ...
CVE-2026-128330.description: Miniflux before 2.3.5 contains an insufficient session expiration vulnerability that allows attackers to retain account access because password changes do not revoke existing web sessions. Attackers holding a leaked password or copied session cookie keep access for up to 30 days, reading integration credentials, creating API keys, or registering passkeys.

CVE-2026-128331.title: Miniflux before 2.3.5 contains an unverified password change vuln ...
CVE-2026-128331.description: Miniflux before 2.3.5 contains an unverified password change vulnerability that allows holders of a signed-in session to change the account password without supplying the current password. Attackers with a stolen session cookie or unattended device can submit new password fields via updateSettings to lock out the owner and take over the account.

CVE-2026-21885.title: Miniflux 2 is an open source feed reader. Prior to version 2.2.16 ...
CVE-2026-21885.description: Miniflux 2 is an open source feed reader. Prior to version 2.2.16, Miniflux's media proxy endpoint (`GET /proxy/{encodedDigest}/{encodedURL}`) can be abused to perform Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF). An authenticated user can cause Miniflux to generate a signed proxy URL for attacker-chosen media URLs embedded in feed entry content, including internal addresses (e.g., localhost, private RFC1918 ranges, or link-local metadata endpoints). Requesting the resulting `/proxy/...` URL makes Miniflux fetch and return the internal response. Version 2.2.16 fixes the issue.

CVE-2026-55185.title: Miniflux 2 is an open source feed reader. Prior to 2.3.1, IsRelat ...
CVE-2026-55185.description: Miniflux 2 is an open source feed reader. Prior to 2.3.1, IsRelativePath in internal/urllib/url.go accepts redirect targets containing backslashes because Go URL parsing treats them as path characters. Browser backslash normalization converts them to forward slashes. An unauthenticated attacker can provide such a redirect_url value to the login flow, bypass the relative-path and host checks, and redirect a victim to an attacker-controlled external site. This issue is fixed in version 2.3.1.

GHSA-fwp7-34mv-hm2r.title: Cross-user IDOR in the UI enclosure save-progression handler (missing ownership check)
GHSA-fwp7-34mv-hm2r.description: ### Summary The web UI endpoint that saves the playback position of a media enclosure did not verify that the enclosure belongs to the authenticated user. Any logged-in user could overwrite the `media_progression` value of another user's enclosure by guessing its sequential ID. The equivalent API endpoint (`PUT /v1/enclosures/{enclosureID}`) was not affected. ### Details `POST /entry/enclosure/{enclosureID}/save-progression` loaded the enclosure by ID without filtering on the current user, then saved the new progression value. ### Proof of Concept Logged in as the attacker, using the attacker's own session and CSRF token: ``` POST /entry/enclosure/{victim_enclosure_id}/save-progression Content-Type: application/json X-Csrf-Token: {attacker_csrf_token} {'progression': 55555} ``` The server returns `201 Created` and updates the other user's enclosure. Because a nonexistent ID returns `404`, the response also shows whether an enclosure ID exists. ### Impact Only affects multi-user instances. An authenticated user can change another user's audio/video resume position. No data is disclosed and no other fields can be modified. ### Patches Fixed in Miniflux 2.3.2. Enclosure lookups are now scoped to the current user.

GHSA-v673-332q-cq35.title: Stored XSS via javascript: URLs in iframe src attributes
GHSA-v673-332q-cq35.description: ### Summary The HTML sanitizer checked `<iframe src>` against a domain allowlist without checking the URL scheme. An iframe such as `<iframe src='javascript://youtube.com/%0Aalert(document.domain)'>` passed the check and was stored unchanged, with `sandbox='allow-scripts allow-same-origin ...'`. ### Details Go's `url.Parse` sets `Host` for any URL with an authority component, whatever the scheme, so `javascript://youtube.com/...` matched the allowlisted `youtube.com`. In a `javascript:` URL, `//youtube.com/` is a line comment and the encoded newline (`%0A`) ends it, so the rest runs as script. Versions 2.0.24 to 2.2.9 also accepted iframe sources on the same host as the entry URL, so the attacker's own domain could be used. ### Impact An attacker who controls a feed the victim subscribes to can run JavaScript in any client that renders entry content from the REST, Fever, or Google Reader API without a Content Security Policy that blocks `javascript:` URLs. The script runs in the client's origin and can, for example, read stored API credentials. The Miniflux web UI is not affected: its Content Security Policy blocks `javascript:` URLs. ### Patches Fixed in 2.3.4 by https://github.com/miniflux/v2/commit/3b5a7ee47bb1605e49c59b49075b74fc6e501af3: iframe sources must use `http`, `https`, or a protocol-relative URL. Content is sanitized when an entry is ingested, so entries stored before upgrading are not cleaned. ### Credits Security research and disclosure by Frederick Stempfle on behalf of whitelisthackers.

GHSA-v673-332q-cq35.description: ### Summary The HTML sanitizer checked `<iframe src>` against a domain allowlist without checking the URL scheme. An iframe such as `<iframe src='javascript://youtube.com/%0Aalert(document.domain)'>` passed the check and was stored unchanged, with `sandbox='allow-scripts allow-same-origin ...'`. ### Details Go's `url.Parse` sets `Host` for any URL with an authority component, whatever the scheme, so `javascript://youtube.com/...` matched the allowlisted `youtube.com`. In a `javascript:` URL, `//youtube.com/` is a line comment and the encoded newline (`%0A`) ends it, so the rest runs as script. Versions 2.0.24 to 2.2.9 also accepted iframe sources on the same host as the entry URL, so the attacker's own domain could be used. ### Impact An attacker who controls a feed the victim subscribes to can run JavaScript in any client that renders entry content from the REST, Fever, or Google Reader API without a Content Security Policy that blocks `javascript:` URLs. The script runs in the client's origin and can, for example, read stored API credentials. The Miniflux web UI is not affected: its Content Security Policy blocks `javascript:` URLs. ### Patches Fixed in 2.3.4 by https://github.com/miniflux/v2/commit/3b5a7ee47bb1605e49c59b49075b74fc6e501af3: iframe sources must use `http`, `https`, or a protocol-relative URL. Content is sanitized when an entry is ingested, so entries stored before upgrading are not cleaned. ### Credits Security research and disclosure by Frederick Stempfle on behalf of whitelisthackers.
